title: Artificial intelligence technologies and applications for language learning and teaching
venue: J. China Comput. Assist. Lang. Learn.
extended_summary:
This paper reviews the literature on artificial intelligence in second and foreign language learning and teaching, asking what major AI technologies and applications have been studied in CALL-related research and what common findings emerge. The authors aim to map trends and synthesize evidence across AI-supported language education, while also identifying gaps and future needs for more rigorous research and better pedagogical implementation.

The review covers seven categories of AI technologies and applications: natural language processing, data-driven learning, automated writing evaluation, computerized dynamic assessment, intelligent tutoring systems, automatic speech recognition, and chatbots. The authors searched CALL-related journals published from 2010 to 2022, along with relevant books and book chapters, and then narratively synthesized findings. The paper includes discussion of teacher perceptions, learner outcomes, feedback systems, autonomy, motivation, and implementation concerns across these categories. ChatGPT is mentioned only briefly in the chatbot section as an emerging tool with potential for language teaching, but it is not the focus of a primary empirical study in this paper.

The populations and contexts represented in the reviewed literature are broad rather than tied to a single sample. The paper references studies involving secondary students, university students, teachers, K-12 learners, and adult language learners across multiple countries and learning settings. Because this is a literature review, it does not report one unified intervention, classroom implementation, or participant group; instead it summarizes many heterogeneous studies spanning classroom, out-of-class, mobile, and online language-learning contexts.

The main conclusions are that AI is becoming increasingly integrated into language education and shows promise for providing feedback, personalization, flexibility, and learner autonomy. At the same time, the review emphasizes persistent concerns about teacher preparedness, pedagogical design, technical limitations, ethics, and the need for stronger evidence. For the user's specific topic, this paper does not provide direct evidence about authentic grades 9-12 classroom use of ChatGPT-generated feedback on student-authored drafts, nor does it report operational details such as prompt design, rubric alignment, feedback cycles, privacy procedures, plagiarism safeguards, or fidelity measures for ChatGPT-based writing feedback.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed narrative literature review, but it does not report a systematic review protocol, meta-analysis, or original causal study. It synthesizes prior work across contexts with limited methodological transparency for evidence grading.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper itself does not estimate an intervention effect or report aggregate effect sizes, so impact is unclear. It offers broad descriptive conclusions that AI shows promise in language education, but these are not tied to a directly measured impact in a defined population.

interventions.use_case: Narrative literature review of AI technologies for second/foreign language learning and teaching, covering NLP, data-driven learning, automated writing evaluation, computerized dynamic assessment, intelligent tutoring systems, ASR, chatbots, and brief commentary on ChatGPT; does not evaluate a single classroom intervention.
Synthesizes studies of automated writing evaluation and automated written corrective feedback for student writing, including feedback on grammar, discourse, and genre features.
Reviews language-learning tools such as Grammarly, machine translation, ASR-supported pronunciation tools, and related AI language supports used in L2/FL learning.
Summarizes research on intelligent computer-assisted language learning and tutoring systems that provide personalized language instruction and corrective feedback.
Briefly discusses chatbots and mentions ChatGPT as a newly emerging AI conversational system with possible implications for education, but without direct empirical evaluation.
